Two relations are available.

  corpus      one row per document in the working sample, WITH the text.
  corpus_meta one row per document in the whole corpus, WITHOUT the text.

Columns (identical in both, except `text`, which only `corpus` has):
  id                    document identifier
  text                  document text (corpus only)
  url, domain           source URL and its host
  dump, date            crawl the document came from, and its timestamp
  language              language label assigned by the corpus pipeline
  language_score        the pipeline's confidence in that label
  minhash_cluster_size  size of the near-duplicate cluster the document
                        represented before deduplication (1 = unique)
  fasttext, langdetect  labels from two independent off-the-shelf language
                        identifiers, shipped with the corpus release
  lingua_top            top language from a third identifier, which reports
                        a distribution over languages within the document
  lingua_top_p          that identifier's proportion for lingua_top
  n_bad_words           number of profanity-list matches recorded by the
                        corpus release
  n_chars, n_words, n_lines  document size
Raw pipeline fields `top_langs` (JSON) and `lingua` (list of
(language, proportion) pairs, as text) are also available on both
relations if you want the full distributions.

input.description:
A large content-farm/doorway-page spam campaign hosted on randomly-named *.firebaseapp.com and *.web.app subdomains (topic-word + random suffix, e.g. akozbohatnutmulk.firebaseapp.com, danexbnl.firebaseapp.com) accounts for a huge share of the corpus. Documents are auto-generated pastiches of unrelated scraped sentence fragments (crypto/finance boilerplate, currency converters, news snippets, search-suggestion queries like "moje heslo je tapeta") stitched together into ~700-1200 word pages with no coherent topic, author or narrative. They pass the language filter because most fragments are genuine Slovak (or Slovak+Czech) sentences, so language_score is typically >0.98 despite the text being incoherent.</description>

input.evidence: domain_stats shows ~2851 distinct spam subdomains under these two suffixes, together 1,408,437 of 26,470,482 documents (5.3% of the corpus overall), concentrated almost entirely in CC-MAIN-2022-49 through CC-MAIN-2023-40 (up to 38.7% of a single dump's Slovak documents, e.g. CC-MAIN-2023-06). minhash_cluster_size averages ~1.0 (each page is near-unique text, so dedup does not catch it) and language_score averages 0.98. Inspected 22 sampled documents (evaluate_detector n=12 seed=7 plus earlier sample n=10 seed=2, plus one full inspect_document read): all were incoherent stitched fragments on finance/crypto/tech/converter topics with no single coherent subject, consistent with automatically generated SEO doorway pages, not human-authored text. Zero documents in the samples looked like genuine articles.
input.likely_false_positives: Essentially none observed among 22 inspected; theoretically a legitimate site could be hosted on Firebase/Google App Engine's free subdomains, but none were seen in samples of this size (topical-keyword-plus-random-suffix domain naming is itself a strong spam signature).
input.assertion: Documents from *.firebaseapp.com / *.web.app doorway-spam domains should be excluded, or at minimum the corpus should not silently contain a 5%+ share of incoherent auto-generated content under a genuine-Slovak-text label.

input.description: A large content-farm/doorway-page spam campaign hosted on randomly-named *.firebaseapp.com and *.web.app subdomains (topic-word + random suffix, e.g. akozbohatnutmulk.firebaseapp.com, danexbnl.firebaseapp.com) accounts for a huge share of the corpus. Documents are auto-generated pastiches of unrelated scraped sentence fragments (crypto/finance boilerplate, currency converters, news snippets, search-suggestion queries like "moje heslo je tapeta") stitched together into ~700-1200 word pages with no coherent topic, author or narrative. They pass the language filter because most fragments are genuine Slovak (or Slovak+Czech) sentences, so language_score is typically >0.98 despite the text being incoherent.
input.evidence: domain_stats shows ~2851 distinct spam subdomains under these two suffixes, together 1,408,437 of 26,470,482 documents (5.3% of the corpus overall), concentrated almost entirely in CC-MAIN-2022-49 through CC-MAIN-2023-40 (up to 38.7% of a single dump's Slovak documents, e.g. CC-MAIN-2023-06). minhash_cluster_size averages ~1.0 (each page is near-unique text, so dedup does not catch it) and language_score averages 0.98. Inspected 22 sampled documents (evaluate_detector n=12 seed=7 plus earlier sample n=10 seed=2, plus one full inspect_document read): all were incoherent stitched fragments on finance/crypto/tech/converter topics with no single coherent subject, consistent with automatically generated SEO doorway pages, not human-authored text. Zero documents in the samples looked like genuine articles.
input.likely_false_positives: Essentially none observed among 22 inspected; theoretically a legitimate site could be hosted on Firebase/Google App Engine's free subdomains, but none were seen in samples of this size (topical-keyword-plus-random-suffix domain naming is itself a strong spam signature).
input.assertion: Documents from *.firebaseapp.com / *.web.app doorway-spam domains should be excluded, or at minimum the corpus should not silently contain a 5%+ share of incoherent auto-generated content under a genuine-Slovak-text label.

input.description:
A systematic slice of documents are substantially or entirely Czech-language text (product data, forum posts, cookie notices, thesis metadata, Pinterest boards) that the corpus nonetheless labels as Slovak (slk_Latn). These typically come from bilingual CZ/SK commerce platforms, cross-posted forums, and Pinterest country mirrors that reuse Czech copy on .sk domains or vice versa.</description>
<parameter name="selector">fasttext='cs' AND langdetect='cs' AND lingua_top='cs' AND NOT (domain LIKE '%.firebaseapp.com' OR domain LIKE '%.web.app')
input.evidence: 44,251 of 26,470,482 documents (0.17%) have all three independent language identifiers (fasttext, langdetect, lingua) agreeing on Czech while the pipeline's own label is Slovak. domain_stats shows this concentrated in identifiable domain classes: Pinterest country mirrors (cz.pinterest.com 9.9% of its own docs, sk.pinterest.com 2.7%), CZ/SK shared e-commerce catalogs (latky-marlen.sk 39%, tenisove-zbozi.cz 51%, sracky.1984.cz 76% -- though the last is actually a nonsense/profanity generator, a separate issue), bilingual parenting/forum sites (modrykonik.sk/.cz), and a Czech thesis repository (dspace.vutbr.cz, 8.7%, though many of these have genuinely Slovak abstracts with only Czech/English metadata labels -- a partial false positive). I inspected 15+15 sampled documents (evaluate_detector seed=9 n=15 and sample_documents seed=3/4): the large majority (~13/15, ~87%) were dominantly or entirely Czech running text (e.g. latky-marlen.sk fabric descriptions in Czech, mandarinka.cz jewelry descriptions in Czech, arome.cz classified ad, audiozone.cz forum reply) with at most a Slovak sentence or two; a minority were genuinely bilingual forum threads (modrykonik) where Slovak and Czech speakers converse in their own language on the same page. I also checked fasttext='cs' alone (without langdetect/lingua agreement): that weaker condition was much noisier, catching many genuinely Slovak pages that fasttext misclassifies on short/quote-heavy text (forum.zdravie.sk, zlavoking.sk, new.rcsolosnica.sk all pure Slovak) -- so I did not use it.
input.likely_false_positives: Genuinely bilingual CZ/SK forum threads where the majority language present may still be Slovak in aggregate across the page; Slovak academic abstracts hosted on Czech institutional repositories (dspace.vutbr.cz) where only template/metadata fields are Czech but the abstract body is authentic Slovak.
input.assertion: Documents where independent language identifiers unanimously disagree with the corpus's Slovak label and agree on Czech should be re-examined and either relabeled or removed from a Slovak-only resource.

Pages are keyword-stuffed concatenations of pornographic video-tag phrases machine-translated/rendered into Slovak, not coherent prose, and repeat the same tag vocabulary across thousands of near-identical URLs per domain.
input.evidence: n_bad_words > 5 selects 52,354 of 26,470,482 documents (0.20%) across 660 distinct domains. domain_stats shows dozens of domains where 40-65% of ALL that domain's documents match this threshold (e.g. adv-moto-girl.bike 63%, accesslocator.net 64%, badotea.info 63%), indicating whole-domain spam rather than incidental profanity. A follow-up aggregate restricting to domains where >15% of the domain's own documents exceed the threshold (and the domain has >50 docs) found 63 such domains totaling 99,008 documents (0.37% of the corpus) -- i.e. the true footprint of this spam network is roughly double what the bad-words threshold alone catches, since many of its pages use euphemisms/fewer flagged terms per page. I inspected 15 sampled documents via evaluate_detector (seed=11): all 15 (100%) were confirmed pornographic-tag doorway pages with no coherent Slovak prose, matching the pattern (e.g. 'Manelka berie prvy vek penis', 'eben-ghetto-sex', keyword strings like 'Sexy čierna eben sluts sex pre monny'). language_score on these was very high (0.99+) since the individual words/phrases are valid Slovak translations, so the language filter does not catch them.

input.description: A third distinct content-farm network: hundreds of unrelated-looking, seemingly hijacked/repurposed domains (e.g. slo.andhramedicalcollegevizag.com, slo.istanbulmedicine.com, slo.kelinvestgroup.com, slo.orsitaning.ru) all serve the same machine-translated content mirror under a 'slo.' (Slovak) subdomain. Content is overwhelmingly pseudo-medical/health/lifestyle articles whose URL slugs are transliterated Russian (e.g. 'diagnostika-raka-jaichek-u-muzhchin', 'kod-po-mkb-mehanicheskaja-zheltuha'), indicating the same Russian-origin article set has been bulk machine-translated into Slovak (and presumably many other languages via sibling subdomain prefixes) and republished across this domain farm. Unlike the firebaseapp.com spam, the translated text is fluent and grammatically coherent single-topic prose, so it reads as legitimate native Slovak and would not be caught by quality heuristics, but it is not organically authored Slovak content and the same articles are repeated near-verbatim across dozens of domains.
input.evidence: 231 distinct domains under the 'slo.' prefix, totaling 73,835 of 26,470,482 documents (0.28% of documents). These documents are far longer than the corpus average (mean 5,060 words vs. corpus-wide mean 438 words, ~11.6x), so they account for a disproportionate ~3.2% of the corpus's total word volume despite being 0.28% of documents. evaluate_detector (seed=6, n=12) inspected 12 sampled documents: all 12 were fluent Slovak health/lifestyle/pet-care articles with Russian-transliterated URL slugs, hosted on domains whose names bear no topical relation to their content (a medical article at 'slo.kelinvestgroup.com', a Nintendo Switch game article at 'slo.gov-civil-lisboa.pt') -- strong evidence of a domain-squatting content-mirror operation rather than genuine publishers. minhash_cluster_size on these documents is mostly 1-6, indicating the near-duplicate detector only partially catches copies of the same underlying article spread across different mirror domains.
input.likely_false_positives: A small number of domains under this prefix could coincidentally be legitimate Slovak-prefixed sites unrelated to the farm; none were observed in the 12-document sample, but the prefix match alone is a heuristic, not a certified membership test.
input.assertion: Bulk machine-translated content republished across a domain-squatting mirror farm should not be included as if it were organic native-language Slovak text; such documents should be deduplicated across domains and/or filtered by their subdomain-mirroring signature.

## Audit summary

I audited the `slk_
Latn` slice (26.47M documents in `corpus_meta`, 2.03M in the working sample) by orienting on
aggregate structure, forming hypotheses from what the data showed, and checking each with targeted sampling before quantifying prevalence. In

spection budget used: ~180/300.

### Findings recorded (4)

1. **`firebase_doorway
_spam_farm`** — **5.32% of the corpus (1,408,437 docs)**. A massive doorway-
page spam campaign on ~2,851 randomly-named `*.firebaseapp.com` / `*.web.app` subdomains (e.g. `akozb
ohatnutmulk.firebaseapp.com`). Pages are incoherent pastiches of sc
raped finance/crypto/tech fragments stitched together — not human-authored text — but pass language filtering because the fragments are gen
uine Slovak/Czech sentences (avg language_score 0.98). Concentrated almost entirely in CC-MAIN-2022-49 through 2023-40
(up to 38.7% of a single dump). Near-unique text per page (minhash_cluster_size≈1), so dedup doesn't cat

ch it. Precision on inspection: ~22/22 confirmed.

2. **`porn_doorway_spam_network`** — **~
0.2–0.37% of the corpus (52k–99k docs)**. A second, unrelated spam network: ~60+ oddly-named domains (`
adv-moto-girl.bike`, `baazzaa.com`, `agencerepublique
.net`, etc.) serving keyword-stuffed pornographic-tag doorway pages machine-translated into Slovak. 15/15 sampled docs confirmed

spam.

3. **`slo_prefix_machine_translated_farm`** — **0.28% of docs but ~3.2% of total word volume (73
,835 docs, avg 5,060 words each vs. 438 corpus-wide)**. A domain-squatting network of 231 `slo.*` subdom
ains on unrelated hijacked-looking domains, republishing the same bulk machine-translated (apparently Russian-origin) health/pseudom
edical articles. Unlike the other two, this text is fluent and coherent, so it reads as legitimate native Slovak but is a

repeated MT mirror, not organic content. 12/12 sampled confirmed.

4. **`czech_text_mislabeled_as_slovak`** — **0.12% of the corpus (31
,795 docs excluding overlap with #1)**. Documents where fasttext, langdetect, and lingua all independently agree on Czech while the p
ipeline labels them Slovak — bilingual CZ/SK e-commerce catalogs, Pinterest mirrors, and cross-posted forums. ~87% of s

ampled docs were substantially/entirely Czech prose.

### Hypotheses investigated and rejected
- **Deduplication failure**: exact-duplicate text in
the sample is negligible (2 pairs out of 2M); large minhash clusters correctly collapse to single representatives —

dedup works as intended.
- **Recurring homepage URLs** (tasr.sk, sme.sk appearing hundreds of times): each sn

apshot has genuinely different headline content, not duplication.
- **Encoding/mojibake corruption**: real but vanishingly rare (~78 docs estimated cor

pus-wide) — not systematic enough.
- **i18n "Translation missing" leakage**: only 5/2M in sample — too rare.
-
**fasttext-alone disagreement as a Czech-detector**: much noisier than the triple-agreement signal, flags many

genuinely Slovak pages (quotes, short boilerplate) — rejected in favor of the triple-agreement selector.
- **Generic free-hosting sp
am** (blogspot/wordpress/wixsite/github.io): checked and found to host ordinary personal blogs, not sp

am — the doorway-farm pattern is specific to firebaseapp.com/web.app.

### What I'd investigate next with more budget
- English-triple-agreement documents (~51k,
0.19%) show a similar but distinct mislabeling pattern (English tourism/e-commerce chrome, product

listings) — likely worth its own finding with more budget rather than folding into the Czech one.
- Whether the
`slo.*` farm has sibling-language subdomain prefixes for other languages, which would confirm the mult

i-language mirror-network theory more rigorously.
- Precision-tightening the por
n-spam selector beyond `n_bad_words>5` (true network footprint estimated ~99k via domain-level thresholding, wor

th confirming with more sampling).
- Lower-frequency near-duplicate leakage from the `slo.*` farm across mirror domains (same article,
different domain) that minhash only partially caught.

## Audit summary

I audited the `slk_Latn` slice (26.47M documents in `corpus_meta`, 2.03M in the working sample) by orienting on aggregate structure, forming hypotheses from what the data showed, and checking each with targeted sampling before quantifying prevalence. Inspection budget used: ~180/300.

### Findings recorded (4)

1. **`firebase_doorway_spam_farm`** — **5.32% of the corpus (1,408,437 docs)**. A massive doorway-page spam campaign on ~2,851 randomly-named `*.firebaseapp.com` / `*.web.app` subdomains (e.g. `akozbohatnutmulk.firebaseapp.com`). Pages are incoherent pastiches of scraped finance/crypto/tech fragments stitched together — not human-authored text — but pass language filtering because the fragments are genuine Slovak/Czech sentences (avg language_score 0.98). Concentrated almost entirely in CC-MAIN-2022-49 through 2023-40 (up to 38.7% of a single dump). Near-unique text per page (minhash_cluster_size≈1), so dedup doesn't catch it. Precision on inspection: ~22/22 confirmed.

2. **`porn_doorway_spam_network`** — **~0.2–0.37% of the corpus (52k–99k docs)**. A second, unrelated spam network: ~60+ oddly-named domains (`adv-moto-girl.bike`, `baazzaa.com`, `agencerepublique.net`, etc.) serving keyword-stuffed pornographic-tag doorway pages machine-translated into Slovak. 15/15 sampled docs confirmed spam.

3. **`slo_prefix_machine_translated_farm`** — **0.28% of docs but ~3.2% of total word volume (73,835 docs, avg 5,060 words each vs. 438 corpus-wide)**. A domain-squatting network of 231 `slo.*` subdomains on unrelated hijacked-looking domains, republishing the same bulk machine-translated (apparently Russian-origin) health/pseudomedical articles. Unlike the other two, this text is fluent and coherent, so it reads as legitimate native Slovak but is a repeated MT mirror, not organic content. 12/12 sampled confirmed.

4. **`czech_text_mislabeled_as_slovak`** — **0.12% of the corpus (31,795 docs excluding overlap with #1)**. Documents where fasttext, langdetect, and lingua all independently agree on Czech while the pipeline labels them Slovak — bilingual CZ/SK e-commerce catalogs, Pinterest mirrors, and cross-posted forums. ~87% of sampled docs were substantially/entirely Czech prose.

### Hypotheses investigated and rejected
- **Deduplication failure**: exact-duplicate text in the sample is negligible (2 pairs out of 2M); large minhash clusters correctly collapse to single representatives — dedup works as intended.
- **Recurring homepage URLs** (tasr.sk, sme.sk appearing hundreds of times): each snapshot has genuinely different headline content, not duplication.
- **Encoding/mojibake corruption**: real but vanishingly rare (~78 docs estimated corpus-wide) — not systematic enough.
- **i18n "Translation missing" leakage**: only 5/2M in sample — too rare.
- **fasttext-alone disagreement as a Czech-detector**: much noisier than the triple-agreement signal, flags many genuinely Slovak pages (quotes, short boilerplate) — rejected in favor of the triple-agreement selector.
- **Generic free-hosting spam** (blogspot/wordpress/wixsite/github.io): checked and found to host ordinary personal blogs, not spam — the doorway-farm pattern is specific to firebaseapp.com/web.app.

### What I'd investigate next with more budget
- English-triple-agreement documents (~51k, 0.19%) show a similar but distinct mislabeling pattern (English tourism/e-commerce chrome, product listings) — likely worth its own finding with more budget rather than folding into the Czech one.
- Whether the `slo.*` farm has sibling-language subdomain prefixes for other languages, which would confirm the multi-language mirror-network theory more rigorously.
- Precision-tightening the porn-spam selector beyond `n_bad_words>5` (true network footprint estimated ~99k via domain-level thresholding, worth confirming with more sampling).
- Lower-frequency near-duplicate leakage from the `slo.*` farm across mirror domains (same article, different domain) that minhash only partially caught.
